intro: An argumentative commentary of about 420 words on the value of reading, with eleven gaps. The first paragraph reports the critics’ thesis in indirect speech: after the single signal „so heißt es seit Jahren in Feuilletons und auf Podien“ every verb stays in the subjunctive – „wer heute noch einen Roman von sechshundert Seiten zur Hand nehme, gelte bereits als Sonderling“. From „Diese Diagnose hat den Vorzug der Eingängigkeit.“ onwards the author speaks in his own voice, in the indicative: he refutes part of the thesis, concedes another part, draws a limited conclusion and ends with „Nicht das Lesen ist bedroht, sondern die Muße, die es verlangt.“ The gaps test the Konjunktiv I and its Konjunktiv II substitute in sustained reported speech, the fixed phrases of refutation and concession, and the author’s hedged claims. Some gaps are drop-down choices, some must be typed; the hint gives the verb or its meaning, never the form.
tips[0].title: Sustained reported speech: the mood is the only marker
tips[0].text: Once a thesis is introduced as someone else’s (so heißt es, die Kritiker behaupten), the following sentences often carry no new reporting verb. Only the subjunctive shows that they are still the critics’ words; an indicative would turn them into the author’s own claim – which he then refutes. Use Konjunktiv I where it differs from the indicative (er nehme, es gelte); where it does not – mostly in the plural – switch to Konjunktiv II. The examples below are parallel sentences, not from the text.
tips[0].trap: Singular subjects normally keep Konjunktiv I (sei, gehe, werde); Konjunktiv II there (ginge, würde) is possible but informal or adds extra doubt. Check the subject too: a plural subject after the verb still needs a plural form.
tips[0].check.why: Plural Konjunktiv I lesen looks like the indicative, so you switch to Konjunktiv II läsen to keep it marked as the critics' words.
tips[0].visual.blocks[0].label: the critics (Konjunktiv I)
tips[0].visual.blocks[1].label: the author (indicative)
tips[1].title: Refuting and conceding in academic register
tips[1].text: The author answers the thesis with fixed phrases: einer Prüfung (nicht) standhalten, sich (kaum) belegen lassen, nicht von der Hand zu weisen sein (a concession), Daraus folgt nicht, dass … (limiting a conclusion), Es kommt vielmehr darauf an, … (his own proposal). Learn them as units – the verb particle belongs to the phrase.
tips[1].check.why: The fixed phrase is sich (kaum) belegen lassen; standhalten needs a dative (einer Prüfung), and weisen belongs to von der Hand weisen.
tips[2].title: The author’s own claims: indicative plus hedging
tips[2].text: nahelegen, dass … is a hedging verb, not a reporting verb: the clause after it stays indicative. The author also grades his certainty with modal verbs used subjectively – dürfte = “is probably”, not “may” in the sense of permission.
tips[2].trap: darf expresses permission; dürfte (Konjunktiv II) expresses probability. dürfe is Konjunktiv I and would mark a reported claim.
tips[2].check.why: dürfte grades the author's own certainty as probable; darf means permission, and dürfe would mark a reported claim.
table.caption: Konjunktiv I or its substitute in reported speech
remember[0]: so heißt es / die Kritiker behaupten → every following verb stays subjunctive until the author takes over.
remember[1]: Konjunktiv I if it differs from the indicative; otherwise Konjunktiv II (hätten, kämen, würden …).
remember[2]: nahelegen, dass / darauf hindeuten, dass + indicative: the author’s own hedged claim.
remember[3]: einer Prüfung standhalten · sich belegen lassen · nicht von der Hand zu weisen · Daraus folgt nicht, dass …
hook: Follow a commentary that reports the critics' view in the subjunctive, then takes it apart in the author's own voice.
